stem: A manufacturer wants to predict bearing failures from vibration sensor streams. Which approach is the most appropriate first choice?

options.text: A general-purpose chat LLM reading raw sensor values
A predictive time-series or anomaly-detection model trained on labelled sensor history, with an LLM at most for explaining alerts
A rules spreadsheet with no data
An image generator

explanation: Sensor streams are numeric time series; purpose-built predictive models are the standard tool. LLMs may help summarise findings but are not the predictor.

stem: Which design principle is most important when adding an AI assistant to a clinical documentation workflow?

options.text: Maximise autonomy
Keep a qualified clinician accountable for content, protect patient data under applicable rules, and make provenance and edits auditable
Hide AI involvement from clinicians
Store transcripts in public storage

explanation: Healthcare settings add patient-safety and privacy duties: human accountability, data protection and audit. Specific obligations depend on jurisdiction and need legal confirmation.

stem: In financial services, which requirement most strongly shapes using ML for credit-related decisions?

options.text: Colour contrast
Explainability, fairness testing, model risk management and an accountable human process around the model
Faster page load
Number of microservices

explanation: Credit decisions are regulated and affect individuals; model governance, explainability and bias testing are central. Exact rules depend on jurisdiction.

stem: A retailer asks for "AI for demand planning" and proposes a chat assistant over sales spreadsheets. Their problem is stock-outs and overstock across 5,000 products.
constraints: Historical sales and promotions data exists
Planners want to understand the forecast

options.text: Use a forecasting model on the historical and promotional data for the numbers, and optionally add an LLM interface that explains forecasts and drivers to planners without producing the numbers itself.
Have the LLM estimate demand from pasted spreadsheets.
Buy more stock to avoid stock-outs.
Build a forecasting model for the numbers but give planners no way to see what drives each forecast.

rationales.text: Quantitative forecasting is a predictive-ML task with measurable error.
An LLM reading spreadsheets gives a validated forecast.
A conversational layer can improve explanation and adoption.

explanation: Match technique to problem: numeric forecasting needs a validated predictive model; an LLM can help with explanation and interaction on top. Forecast error should be measured.
model_answer: Build and validate a forecasting model on historical and promotional data, measure error, and optionally add a conversational explanation layer.

rubric.criterion: Chooses predictive model for the numbers

stem: A logistics firm wants an agent that re-plans deliveries when disruptions occur. Re-planning affects contracts and driver schedules.

options.text: Use the existing optimisation solver for route decisions, let the agent gather context and propose options, require dispatcher approval for contract-affecting changes, and log decisions.
Let the LLM compute routes itself.
Remove human involvement to react faster.
Ban AI from logistics.

rationales.text: Solvers are purpose-built for optimisation; models should not replace them.
Approval gates limit the cost of wrong changes.

explanation: Combine deterministic optimisation with an agent for context and options, keeping humans in the loop for consequential changes.
model_answer: Call the solver for routes, use the agent to collect disruption data and explain options, require approval for contractual impacts, and audit.
